intro: Seven miles north of Sedona in Oak Creek Canyon, Slide Rock State Park keeps the apple orchard Frank Pendley started in 1912. Apples were the Pendley family's cash crop, and the homestead became a state park in 1987. The orchard, nearly 300 trees by the park's count, is still tended, and in April the whole planting is in blossom. Not every tree dates from 1912; the age belongs to the orchard as a whole.

question_answer: The oldest trees we map near Sedona are those of the Pendley apple orchard at Slide Rock State Park, in Oak Creek Canyon, where Frank Pendley made his first plantings in 1912. That makes the orchard more than a century old. The park does not say how many of today's nearly 300 trees are originals, so the age is the orchard's rather than any one tree's.

trees.story:
Frank Pendley planted his first apple trees in Oak Creek Canyon in 1912, and the orchard has stood on his homestead ever since. Apples were the Pendley family's cash crop. Today the homestead is Slide Rock State Park, and the orchard, nearly 300 trees by the park's count, is still worked.

This is an orchard, not a single tree, and the honest thing to say is that not every tree in it dates from 1912. The park does not say how many of the original plantings survive, so the age belongs to the orchard rather than to any one trunk you stand beside.

The homestead became a state park in 1987, and in 2007 Arizona State Parks took the orchard's care back into its own hands. So the orchard has seen this stretch of canyon turn from a family farm into a state park, and it still flowers every spring.

Come in April, when the blossom is out, and you see the whole planting at once. The park charges an entry fee, and there is no public transport from Sedona; it is a drive of about seven miles north on US 89A. Floods closed the road and the park in early November 2026, so check the park's page before you set out.
